newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bonds positive on stronger German mark.
newsitem.headline: Danish bonds positive on stronger German mark.

text.p: The Danish bond market was in positive mood on Tuesday, bolstered by a strengthening of the German mark against the dollar, with focus on upcoming U.S. consumer confidence and employment cost data.
"The market is not worried about the US data too much. The German mark's strengthening against the dollar has seemingly warded off the risk of any German rate hike," one dealer said.

The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was up a marginal 0.04 point from the opening at 114.29, yielding 5.83 percent. The seven percent 2007, due to be benchmark on Sept 1, was 0.04 point higher at 107.24, with yield at 6.02 percent.
Turnover in the 2006 and 2007 bonds was 2.2 billion and 1.2 billion crowns respectively.
The 2006's September future rose 0.29 point to 113.82 with 50 contracts traded. The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 gained 0.27 point to 93.00.
The crown traded at an unaltered 3.8075 per mark at 1145 GMT. The 10-year yield gap with Germany was unchanged at 50 basis points from Monday's close.
